summary: A 1927 D-6 cupola lookout on Dutchman Peak in the Rogue River National Forest, described as the last original cupola lookout still in use, with a 1937 CCC garage.

facts.design: D-6 cupola cabin, standard wood-frame structure

access.note: Reached by road in summer; a stop on the Mt. Ashland Loop Road. Whether the cabin interior is open to visitors is not confirmed. Ask the Applegate Ranger District.

visit.trail_note: A short distance from the Pacific Crest Trail

events.note: Built as a D-6 cupola lookout; the nomination says a worker posted in summer 1927 most likely built it
CCC crew of five built a garage and woodshed below the lookout
CCC garage converted to a residence for Aircraft Warning Service observers
Registered August 2, 1991 as US 19, OR 5; nominated by Barbara Mumblo, USFS
Forest Service historic preservation team repaired the foundation and installed a new roof

notes_for_editor: Built date and CCC garage, 1942 AWS conversion and 1999 repair come from the NRHP nomination, the strongest source. Current staffing is unverified: firelookout.com is undated and says staffed in summer; IJPR (2017) uses present tense. No 2025-26 schedule found. Summit elevation differs across sources (7,364, 7,417, 7,418 ft); the record's 2244.5 m matches the register's 7,364 ft. The record's access 'unknown' can be set to public per the sources, but whether the cabin interior is open to visitors is not confirmed. A trail-guide claim that the lookout is still used for emergency fire detection was seen only in a search snippet and not used.
